_about.purpose: Hand-labeled exact-span gold standard for the entity extractor. Scored by literature/scorer.py with the same exact-span rule the thesis pipeline uses.
_about.labeling_rule: Spans are labeled for what a CORRECT extractor should find, independent of what the bundled gazetteer actually finds. Several named binders below are deliberately absent from the gazetteer, so the measured recall reflects a real limitation rather than a circular self-check.

splits.demo_corpus: Sentences from the bundled offline corpus. The gazetteer was written against this text, so treat these scores as an in-domain ceiling, not evidence of generalization.
splits.heldout_realistic: Held-out sentences written in the notation and phrasing of real published abstracts, using binders and constructions the gazetteer was NOT built around. This is the honest generalization estimate.

types_not_evaluated: SPARSITY_SIGNAL — a soft discourse cue, not a span two annotators would agree on; reported as not evaluated rather than scored as zero.
_about.offsets: Computed at load time from (text, n) where n is the 0-based occurrence index. The loader asserts the recovered substring matches, so a typo fails loudly instead of silently shifting every span.

sentences.text: Trastuzumab is a humanized monoclonal antibody that binds domain IV of the HER2/ERBB2 extracellular region with sub-nanomolar affinity, reported around 0.1 to 5 nanomolar depending on assay format.
Pertuzumab binds a distinct epitope in domain II and is often used in combination for complementary blockade of HER2 dimerization.
Several single-domain (VHH) binders selected against HER2 domain IV have been reported with affinities in the low nanomolar to sub-nanomolar range.
Cetuximab binds domain III of the EGFR extracellular region and blocks ligand binding, with reported affinities typically in the 1 to 10 nanomolar range across BLI and SPR studies.
Necitumumab and panitumumab bind overlapping or adjacent epitopes with comparable affinity.
Nanobody and scFv binders selected against EGFR domain III typically fall in the low nanomolar range; affinities below 100 picomolar are uncommon in the published literature for this epitope.
Atezolizumab and durvalumab bind the IgV domain of PD-L1 and block the PD-1/PD-L1 interaction, with reported affinities in the sub-nanomolar to low nanomolar range in most published assays.
Engineered small binder scaffolds against the PD-L1 IgV domain have been reported with affinities from roughly 0.5 to 20 nanomolar.
Certain full-length IgG antibodies against the target's extracellular domain bind with affinities reported around 10 to 50 nanomolar in several validated studies.
Engineered nanobody and VHH binders against the same extracellular domain have been reported with sub-nanomolar affinity, in some cases approaching 100 picomolar.
The lead clone bound recombinant antigen with KD = 2.3 nM by surface plasmon resonance, with a 1:1 Langmuir fit.
Rituximab, a chimeric anti-CD20 antibody, engages a large extracellular loop epitope and was used here as the reference binder.
Affinity maturation improved the scFv from 151 nM to 4.6 nM, a roughly 33-fold gain.
Bevacizumab neutralises its ligand rather than a receptor ectodomain, and is therefore not a suitable comparator for domain III binders.
Two nanobodies bound with dissociation constants of 0.39 nM and 3.89 nM respectively.
Obinutuzumab is a glycoengineered type II antibody that binds a partially overlapping epitope.
Binding was weak, with an apparent KD of 1.2 µM under the conditions tested.
Gold nanoparticles of 0.8 nm diameter were conjugated to the binder prior to imaging.
Samples were eluted in 2 M NaCl and dialysed against 10 mM Tris before analysis.
An affibody scaffold selected against domain I showed 15 nM affinity, weaker than the domain III binders.
The VHH retained sub-picomolar apparent affinity in a bivalent format, consistent with avidity rather than true monovalent binding.
